plain_statement: Emergency shelter programs must not exclude people with disabilities, and generally cannot require them to go to a special-needs or medical shelter instead of a regular shelter.
applies_when: When you are at or seeking emergency shelter.

plain_statement: Shelters must change "no pets" rules so people are not separated from their service animals.
applies_when: When you are at or seeking emergency shelter.

plain_statement: Shelters run by state or local government must communicate effectively with people who are blind, deaf, or hard of hearing.
applies_when: When you are at or seeking emergency shelter.

plain_statement: You can file an ADA grievance if the City of Boston discriminated against you because of a disability or did not give you access to meetings, services, programs, or activities. The Disabilities Commission contacts you within 30 days.
applies_when: When the City of Boston denied access because of a disability.

plain_statement: Boston has an ADA Curb Ramp Request Form for corners where a curb ramp is missing or does not meet ADA rules. Contacting the Disabilities Commission can help accessibility-related 311 requests get followed up.
applies_when: When a street corner is missing a curb ramp or it does not meet ADA rules.

plain_statement: For disasters declared on or after March 22, 2024, FEMA can pay for accessibility items such as ramps, grab bars, and paved pathways for a disaster-damaged home, even if they were not there before, and this does not count against the housing assistance maximum. You may be eligible; FEMA decides.
applies_when: After a federally declared disaster affecting your area.

plain_statement: FEMA Other Needs Assistance can help with disaster-caused medical costs, including lost medication and medical equipment.
applies_when: After a federally declared disaster affecting your area.

plain_statement: Since March 2024, people who apply after the 60-day window can give an explanation for the delay instead of supporting documents.
applies_when: After a federally declared disaster affecting your area.

plain_statement: Apply or ask questions by calling the FEMA helpline at 1-800-621-3362, or at DisasterAssistance.gov.
applies_when: After a federally declared disaster affecting your area.

plain_statement: You have the right to appeal a FEMA decision; the decision letter states the deadline.
applies_when: After a federally declared disaster affecting your area.
